proof.title: Before and after training
proof.subtitle: Here the measure is error rate, not cost: that is what separates improvement from luck.
proof.disclaimer: A verdict only appears when the difference survives the confidence interval, and the "before" is corrected so improvement is not inflated. This compares two periods; it does not prove the training caused the change.

explain.melhorou: You used to err {{antes}}% (adjusted to {{ajustado}}% because this leak entered the plan for being the worst of a list, and part of that bad result was luck). Now {{depois}}% over {{n}} decisions. The 95% interval of the drop is [{{lo}} · {{hi}}] and does not touch zero, so the difference survives chance. This compares two periods; it does not prove training caused it.
explain.piorou: You used to err {{antes}}% (adjusted to {{ajustado}}%) and now err {{depois}}% over {{n}} decisions. The 95% interval is [{{lo}} · {{hi}}], entirely negative, so the regression is not noise. The leak was reopened for training.
explain.sem_mudanca: From {{antes}}% (adjusted to {{ajustado}}%) to {{depois}}% over {{n}} decisions. The 95% interval is [{{lo}} · {{hi}}] and crosses zero, so the difference is still indistinguishable from chance. This does NOT mean you did not improve: it means this data cannot say yet.

purity.pure: error rate in spots where GTO plays almost always the same thing, i.e. where there is ONE right answer

proof.purityHint: Zero here is expected, not a merit: in these spots getting it right is range memory, not reading. What measures play is the mixed spots.
proof.purityHintErrs: Each of these is a play GTO makes less than 10% of the time, in a spot with a single answer. That is an unmemorized range, not a hard decision, and it is the cheapest kind of leak to fix.
proof.mixedNote: In mixed spots you had {{erros}} errors over {{n}} decisions. That number does NOT compare to the one above: there GTO accepts more than one action, so erring requires picking a third it never plays. It is harder to err by construction, not because the spot is easier.

export.notesTitle: How to read this file, and what was left out
export.noteScope: Only decisions with a solver answer are counted. A hand with no coverage shows up neither as correct nor as a mistake, so the totals here are smaller than the number of hands you played.
export.noteEv: The bb cost uses only EV that passes the reliability test. An out-of-scale estimate is discarded rather than added, which makes this number a floor: the real cost is equal or higher.
export.noteIcm: The ICM zone (bubble and final table) is excluded from both sides. The reference there is pure chipEV, and the EV measured does not describe the decision you actually faced.
export.noteFrozen: These numbers are from the moment the file was generated and do not update. For today's reading, open the report on the site.
